sec: Hypothyroidism management: levothyroxine and special populations

items.q: Match the following principles of levothyroxine therapy — 1) Form 2) Dosing starting point 3) Administration timing 4) Monitoring interval … A) Oral levothyroxine (tablets) B) Weight-based 1.6 µg/kg in young, low in elderly/cardiac C) Empty stomach, before breakfast D) 6–8 weeks after dose change
items.exp: Oral levothyroxine is given once daily on an empty stomach; full replacement is 1.6 µg/kg in healthy young adults, lower in elderly or cardiac patients; TSH is rechecked 6–8 weeks after dose changes. (Book p908)

items.q: A 30-year-old woman with overt hypothyroidism is started on levothyroxine 100 µg daily. What monitoring schedule fits the source?
opts: Check TSH 6–8 weeks after each dose change
Check TSH monthly for the first year
No monitoring needed once symptoms improve
items.exp: TSH is checked 6–8 weeks after every dose change until stable, then every 6–12 months. (Book p908)

items.q: Evaluate levothyroxine administration: I It should be taken with breakfast for best absorption. II Calcium and iron supplements reduce its absorption.
items.exp: Levothyroxine is taken on an empty stomach 30–60 minutes before breakfast; calcium, iron, antacids and certain foods reduce its absorption. (Book p908)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — a drug that reduces levothyroxine absorption?
items.exp: Methimazole is an antithyroid drug, not an absorption blocker; calcium, iron and PPIs all interfere with levothyroxine uptake. (Book p908)

items.q: In healthy young adults, the typical full replacement dose of levothyroxine is approximately ___ µg/kg/day.
items.exp: Approximately 1.6 µg/kg/day in young healthy adults; lower doses in elderly or ischaemic heart disease. (Book p908)

items.q: Match the following patient group with the source's levothyroxine starting approach — 1) Young healthy adult 2) Elderly 3) Ischaemic heart disease 4) Pregnancy … A) Full weight-based dose B) Start low (25–50 µg), titrate slowly C) Start very low, titrate by 12.5 µg D) Increase dose 25–30% over pre-pregnancy dose
items.exp: Young healthy adults receive full weight-based replacement; elderly start low and titrate slowly; cardiac patients start very low and increment by 12.5 µg; pregnancy increases the dose by 25–30%. (Book p908)

items.q: An 80-year-old with atrial fibrillation and overt hypothyroidism needs levothyroxine. The best initial regimen is:
opts: 200 µg daily as a stat dose
items.exp: Start low in elderly cardiac patients (25–50 µg) and titrate by 12.5–25 µg every 6–8 weeks to avoid precipitating ischaemia. (Book p908)

items.q: Assess thyroid replacement endpoints: I In primary hypothyroidism the target is normal TSH. II In central hypothyroidism the target is normal free T4 only.
items.exp: Primary hypothyroidism uses TSH as the target; central hypothyroidism uses free T4 in the upper normal range because TSH is unreliable. (Book p908)

items.q: Match the following special population to its TSH target on levothyroxine — 1) Young adult 2) Pregnancy (T1) 3) Elderly with cardiac disease 4) Pregnancy (T3) … A) 0.5–2.5 mIU/L B) 0.5–3.0 mIU/L C) Up to 4–6 mIU/L acceptable D) 0.5–2.5 mIU/L
items.exp: Young adults aim for 0.5–2.5; both trimesters of pregnancy aim for similar low targets (T1 stricter); elderly with cardiac disease may tolerate slightly higher TSH. (Book p908)

items.q: A pregnant woman on levothyroxine 100 µg now needs an increased dose. By what percentage should the source's guidance recommend an increase?
items.exp: Pregnancy increases thyroxine requirement by 25–30%; dose should be adjusted once pregnancy is confirmed. (Book p908)

items.q: The source's preferred thyroid hormone preparation is ___, with ___ reserved for selected refractory cases.
items.exp: Levothyroxine is the standard; liothyronine is occasionally added in refractory cases but routine combination therapy is not standard. (Book p908)

items.q: Assess therapeutic drug interactions: I Levothyroxine absorption is reduced by sucralfate. II Cholestyramine reduces levothyroxine absorption.
items.exp: Sucralfate, cholestyramine, calcium, iron and PPIs all reduce levothyroxine absorption; separate dosing by at least four hours. (Book p908)
